keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row: Tashkent and its oasis (an 80 km radius, about 17,000 km2); the pages give no area. YK: the southern and western borders followed the Syr Darya; 'The total population of the Tashkent city itself, by the end of the 18th century, was slightly more than 40 thousand people'.

correction.text: Tashkent plus the Senior Jüz steppes to Chimkent and Turkestan, 'the conquest of the Kazakh steppes was completed in 1798' (YK, citing Pospelov)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Chimkent and Turkestan radii (about 40,000 km2 for the three) are a floor for the steppe authority; the whole domain held 150,000-200,000 people, mostly nomads (YK).

region.text: Tashkent and its oasis, whose four quarters Yunus Khoja united in 1784

ledger.note: 1784: Yunus Khoja unites Tashkent. 'In 1784, the rivalry of the four parts of Tashkent resulted in an armed clash'; 'The conflict was won by Yunus Khoja, and his authority was recognized over the whole city'; 'It was declared in 1784'.

region.text: the Senior Jüz steppes between Chimkent in the north-east and Turkestan in the north, which Yunus Khoja governed through his own appointees (YK)

ledger.note: 1798: the Kazakh steppes of the Senior Jüz are conquered. 'Pospelov's report indicates that the conquest of the Kazakh steppes was completed in 1798'; 'After conquering the Senior Jüz, Yunus-Khoja abolished the khanate title and governed the Senior Jüz through his own appointees'. The region (Chimkent to Turkestan) is the page's description of the border.

region.text: Tashkent and the Senior Jüz steppes

ledger.note: 1809: Kokand annexes Tashkent. 'In 1809, Tashkent was annexed to the Khanate of Kokand.' YK says the state 'ceased to exist in 1808, after being occupied by the Kokand Khanate' and TK dates the state 1784-1807; 1809 follows the khanate-of-kokand dossier.

wars.name: Kokand conquest of Tashkent
wars.outcome: Kokand occupied Tashkent (1808 on YK) and annexed it (1809 on TK); the state ended.
wars.note: YK gives no war, only the occupation by Kokand; the wars with Narbuta Bi, Alim Khan, Bukhara and the Kazakhs are not on the pages.

certainty.note: The oasis edge and the steppe authority are described, not surveyed; the Syr Darya bounds the south and west.

sources.title: Yunus Khoja
sources.note: Declared 1784 after the clash of the four parts of Tashkent; ceased 1808 when occupied by Kokand; the Senior Jüz conquered by 1798; borders on the Syr Darya, Turkestan and Chimkent; population.

sources.title: Tashkent
sources.note: "created an independent Tashkent state (1784-1807)"; Kazakh Khanate 1598-1723; "In 1809, Tashkent was annexed to the Khanate of Kokand"; Russian capture May 1865.

notes: Written for batch ia-03-x from two pages (YK, TK; budget 2-5). Disagreement on the end: YK 'ceased to exist in 1808, after being occupied by the Kokand Khanate'; TK 'independent Tashkent state (1784-1807)' and 'In 1809, Tashkent was annexed to the Khanate of Kokand'. 1809 is used so that the handover matches the khanate-of-kokand dossier (gain 1809, counterpart tashkent-state). Not on the pages: Yunus Khoja's death, the wars with Narbuta Bi and Alim Khan, the 1810s. The Senior Jüz steppe is recorded as a gain from the kazakh-khanate row at confidence 2; the kazakh-khanate dossier (ia-03-a) lists Tashkent as a counterpart under the suggested slug tashkent-state-of-yunus-khoja, while the Kokand dossier uses tashkent-state, which is followed here.
